pending.title: micro1: Mathlib Contributor
pending.description:
Mathlib Contributor
Pay: $60–$120/hour equivalent, paid per accepted task
Location: Global, fully remote
Job Type: Contractor
Time Commitment: 15+ hours per week
Schedule: Flexible
micro1 is looking for contributors with publicly verifiable mathlib experience to support a project focused on improving advanced AI systems.
You will use your experience with mathlib and Lean 4 to create challenging formalization tasks, write machine-checked reference solutions, evaluate generated proofs, and establish objective standards for correct solutions.
This opportunity is intended for mathematics researchers, Lean developers, formalization specialists, and open-source contributors. Prior professional AI-training experience is not required.
What You’ll Work On
Create mathematical and technical tasks based on realistic Lean 4 workflows.
Translate informal requirements into precise definitions, theorem statements, and acceptance criteria.
Write complete, machine-checked reference proofs using appropriate mathlib conventions.
Evaluate generated Lean code for mathematical correctness, technical validity, and alignment with the intended problem.
Public Proof of Skill
Strong applicants should provide evidence such as:
Merged mathlib pull requests or commits
Substantive Lean 4 repositories or formalization projects
Mathlib reviews or open-source maintenance work
Lean tactics, infrastructure, documentation, or testing contributions
Research papers, theses, or technical materials involving Lean
Contributions to other established Lean projects
Please provide your GitHub username and links to your strongest mathlib contributions.
Preferred Qualifications
Multiple substantive mathlib contributions.
Experience reviewing or maintaining other contributors’ Lean code.
Experience contributing across mathematical proofs, tactics, infrastructure, or other technical areas of mathlib.
Application Process
Submit your application and GitHub username.
Provide links to your strongest mathlib contributions.
Complete an AI interview covering contribution ownership, mathlib expertise, and programming.
If experience is relevant, you'll be moved to hiring-manager review.
If selected, complete onboarding and begin your first assigned task.
Compensation
Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid for tasks that meet project specifications and quality requirements. Task availability and completion time may vary.

pending.title: G2i Inc.: Senior Software Engineer, AI Training
pending.description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details: 
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

pending.title: micro1: Inpatient facility coder
pending.description:
Role Title: Inpatient facility coderRole Type: ContractorLocation: Remote
micro1 is engaging experienced Inpatient facility coders to contribute to a customer project focused on high-quality case review and adjudication. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters. This engagement emphasizes strong written and verbal communication, attention to detail, and a commitment to coding excellence.
Scope of Work
Review and code inpatient facility stays using ICD-10-CM and PCS classifications, ensuring accurate MS-DRG and APR-DRG assignment.
Conduct comprehensive pre-bill reviews, DRG validation, and second-level audits as part of case adjudication.
Document clear, concise rationales for DRG changes, supported by thorough chart evidence and clinical documentation.
Leverage Epic and industry-standard encoders (3M/Solventum or Optum) during the coding and review process.
Assess cases objectively—calling them up or down as appropriate—and provide detailed written feedback.
Participate in steady case volume review through Q1, meeting project submission requirements and quality benchmarks.
Collaborate remotely with the micro1 platform and project stakeholders to ensure alignment on deliverables and outcomes.
Preferred Qualifications
Active CCS credential required; CIC, RHIT, or RHIA certifications are a plus.
Minimum of 3 years' experience independently coding inpatient stays, including MS-DRG and APR-DRG assignment.
Demonstrated experience in pre-bill review, DRG validation, or second-level coding audits.
Background in clinical validation (CCDS, CDIP, or RN with coding expertise) highly valued.
Proficiency with Epic EHR and at least one standard encoder platform (3M/Solventum or Optum).
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; able to articulate coding decisions and evidence clearly.
Strong analytical mindset and commitment to accuracy, integrity, and ongoing learning within inpatient facility coding.
